features: 7 weapons, each with its own projectile behaviour (the 14 pack variants were retired in 2.4.0)
25 total enemy types with late-run role diversity
5 biomes, one per boss cycle, each with its own floor, props, border, particles, light, hazard and enemy mix
59 run upgrades including 13 evolutions, no duplicates (2.5.0 folded 19 copies into the originals)
18 persistent workshop modules
extended long-term milestones through wave 200 and high lifetime totals
dynamic wave director with 12+ encounter modes
procedural wave-specific obstacle additions with connectivity validation
dynamic vents, ice, acid pools, portals and supply caches; about five large hazards per wave
mode-specific enemy pool injections on later waves
biome-specific champion pools
high-wave scaling and boss progression retained
centralized v2.2 stat integration for new upgrades
additional weapon evolution synergies
new enemy behaviors for drone, driller, beacon and weaver
wave cache economy and persistent salvage interactions
Nova start-charge workshop progression
mobile pointer-id-aware synthetic-click suppression
viewport/orientation changes cancel active gameplay touch captures
resize/orientation follow-up timers are coalesced
bounded save parsing and snapshot sanitization retained
geometry-safe procedural spawn fallbacks retained
deterministic seeded wave and layout generation
runtime post-run diagnostics for arena, entities, input and errors
versioned game bundle and service-worker cache contract
orientation-any PWA manifest
browser-safe offline cache with mandatory core asset verification
expanded deterministic QA for weapons, enemies, waves, layouts and upgrades
25 enemy types with dedicated models
enemy and boss skins per biome
one boss per biome (5 bosses), Void Core and the Rift Core always last
one biome event per visit of a hazard biome: Meltdown, Whiteout, Spore Bloom, Rift Storm
signature enemies of a biome appear from its first wave
biome title card and boss intro card
Codex in Records: enemies, bosses and upgrades you have seen
updates apply on their own outside a run
5 biome music themes
run history in Records
first-encounter enemy hints
live run monitor + post-run audit
tutorial and tips follow the input in use (keyboard/mouse or touch)
keyboard upgrade choice, settings from the pause menu, upgrade details in the pause build
optional run timer and FPS counter
changes: 2.5.1: code refactor, no change to the game: the patches of the content packs and later fixes (methods wrapped from outside, up to eight times each) are folded into the classes and functions, so every method is in one place
2.5.1: about 3,600 minified local names (t, e, n …) are readable names; the minifier's syntax tricks (!0, comma chains, a && f() as a statement, var) are plain statements
2.5.1: the deep self-test has its own module (core/selftest.js); window.__riftTest uses the real names; Prettier formats the code and CI checks it
2.5.1: the save-sanitize health check expected the old High-Yield maximum 8 and reported FAIL since 2.5.0; it reads the maximum from the upgrade now

2.5.0: upgrades without duplicates — 19 weaker copies are folded into the upgrade they copied (e.g. Overbore Caliber and Kinetic Matrix into High-Yield Rounds, Afterburner and Cryo Coolant into Vector Capacitor, which now also shortens the Aegis cooldown); the kept upgrades have higher maximums, so a build reaches about the same totals. 59 upgrades, 13 evolutions unchanged

2.5.0: six new upgrades with their own mechanic — Cryo Skates (faster on ice and in Cryo Vault), Acid Coating (hits leave your own cyan acid, enemies in it take +25%), Heat Sink (fire-rate burst and Nova charge near lava or acid), Slipstream (+25% damage after a dash), Combo Surge (longer combos, a shockwave every 15 combo kills), Reactive Plating (a hit releases a repulse wave, -8% fire rate)

2.5.0: workshop — Rift Battery and Reactor Core are merged into Nova Cell (4 levels, at least 25% Nova per level at the start of each wave), Route Scanner into Field Supply (+1 cache and +50% cache shards per level); bought levels of the removed modules are refunded in full

2.5.0: three new workshop modules — Starter Kit (a random common upgrade per level at the start of a run), Hazard Attunement (+10% damage and +0.5 HP/s near a map hazard per level), Emergency Shield (once per wave below 30% hull: a short barrier and a repair)

2.5.0: stronger biomes — about five hazards per wave instead of three, about 25–30% larger (vents 1.7–2.2, ice 2.7–3.7, acid 2.2–3.0), kept clear of obstacles and further from the spawn; Void Core has two portal pairs in most waves

2.5.0: biome events, one per visit of a hazard biome (waves 2–4 of the visit, never a boss wave, +25% shards): Meltdown (Ember Works, extra vents that erupt together), Whiteout (Cryo Vault, snow storm with dense fog and more ice), Spore Bloom (Toxin Marsh, pools grow and new ones sprout), Rift Storm (Void Core, portals jump to new spots, shown 1.6 s ahead)
2.5.0: the signature enemies of a biome can appear from its first wave (at half weight until their normal unlock wave); Neon Yard is unchanged
2.5.0: biome title card on wave 1 and every biome change (name, hazard, boss) and a boss intro card during the camera pan to a new boss

2.5.0: Codex tab in Records — every enemy, boss and upgrade; the ones you have seen show their description, the others ???; old saves count defeated bosses, builds in the history and the saved run as seen
2.5.0: old saves and runs saved mid-way keep working — levels of removed upgrades become levels of the kept one, removed upgrades in a pending offer are replaced

2.4.6: bigger hazards so they shape the fight — per wave the hazard area grows about ×3 (lava vents), ×5 (acid pools) and ×8 (ice sheets); same number per wave, still placed clear of obstacles and the spawn

2.4.6: every biome has its own boss — Neon Yard: The Warden, Ember Works: The Crucible (new), Cryo Vault: Frost Prism, Toxin Marsh: Hive Queen, Void Core: Rift Core; the boss hull follows its slot (wave 5/10/15/20), so each boss is fair at wave 10 or 15

2.4.6: route — waves 1–5 Neon Yard, 6–15 two of Ember Works, Cryo Vault and Toxin Marsh in a seeded order, 16–20 always Void Core (the Rift Core stays the final boss), the third from wave 21 in Endless

2.4.6: The Crucible — furnace golem with Forge Hammer (slam + fissures + slag ring), Slag Rain, Eruption rings, Furnace Blast and Stoke (bombers/brutes); its arena keeps three lava vents that its attacks make burst
2.4.6: Frost Prism — ice golem model; Frost Beam, Ice Lances, Ice Shards, new Frost Nova and Glacier (telegraphed zones that chill the drone for 1.6 s, a dash avoids them)
2.4.6: Hive Queen — her eggs leave short-lived acid puddles
2.4.6: milestones Icebreaker (Frost Prism) and Quenched (new, The Crucible); title shows 5 bosses
2.4.6: no "New version ready" bar — an update is applied on its own when no run is going on (at start, back in the menu, or when the page is hidden in the menu), never during a run

2.4.5: readable names for the 216 minified top-level names of the original bundle and the 46 three.js classes (Aa → World, ft → game, Ft → ui, ee → store, nr → computeStats, Ct → BoxGeometry …), renamed with scope analysis so no local variable is captured; the game plays exactly as before (determinism test identical)

2.4.4: the game code is split into 21 ES modules (src/main.js, core/, data/, render/, audio/, ui/) instead of one 16 000-line file; the code itself is unchanged apart from imports/exports and five setters where one module assigns a variable of another; the game plays exactly as before

2.4.4: tests/determinism.mjs (part of npm test) compares fixed-seed simulations, stat computations, arena layouts, wave plans and data tables with a golden file, so a refactor cannot change game behaviour unnoticed

2.4.3: three.js comes from npm (three 0.186.0, r186) instead of being embedded in src/game.js; the embedded copy was checked to be unmodified r186 first. src/game.js shrinks from 39 769 to 16 129 lines; the game plays exactly as before
2.4.3: build.js bundles src/game.js with three.js (esbuild bundle instead of transform)
2.4.2: a run that is already lost or won is settled when the page is hidden; closing or reloading in the 1.5 s before the game-over screen used to bring the run back and skip the death
2.4.2: letters are read by their position on the keyboard, so W A S D, E, Q and F sit in the same place on every layout (on AZERTY, Q moved left and fired the Nova as well)
2.4.2: upgrade choice by keyboard — 1–4 pick a card, R rerolls; the cards and the reroll button show the keys
2.4.2: Esc goes back in Workshop, Records and Settings, and also works while a settings toggle has focus
2.4.2: Settings can be opened from the pause menu (without backup and reset); Esc or Back returns to the pause menu
2.4.2: the build in the pause menu explains each upgrade (level and effect) on tap or click
2.4.2: optional run timer and FPS counter in the HUD (Settings → Display)
2.4.2: imported saves apply their settings at once (volume, left-handed, graphics, camera needed a reload)
2.4.2: Auto graphics steps the resolution back up after 20 s at 57+ fps; a short stutter lowered it until the next reload
2.4.2: Last Stand Plating no longer raises hits below 1 damage (acid ticks with high hazard resistance) to 1
2.4.2: full QA has a new section qol for these fixes

2.4.1: enemies and bosses wear the biome — a shader skin over every model (Ember Works: charred shell with pulsing lava veins; Cryo Vault: frost on the upper surfaces with glints; Toxin Marsh: slime and glowing toxic spots; Void Core: violet rim glow and star specks) plus matching particles (embers, frost flakes, drops, motes); type colours and glow stay, so types are still told apart; visual only
2.4.1: tests/biome-shots.mjs spawns a ring of enemies and the boss in every biome and fails on shader compile errors

2.4.0: 5 biomes instead of 19, and the biome changes after every boss again (every wave since 2.1): waves 1–5 Neon Yard, then Ember Works, Cryo Vault, Toxin Marsh and Void Core in a seeded order, one per boss cycle; Endless reaches the fifth at wave 21

2.4.0: each biome looks different, not just differently coloured — own floor (neon grid, basalt with lava seams, frozen sheet, mud and murky water, hex tiles over a starfield), own props on the same collision shapes (pylons/crates, chimneys/machines, crystal clusters/ice blocks, mushrooms/dead trees/logs, floating obelisks/monoliths), own border, ambient particles, sun colour and fog

2.4.0: each biome plays differently — Ember Works favours heavy and explosive enemies, Cryo Vault has a slick floor (you drift) and shielded/ranged enemies, Toxin Marsh swarms, Void Core fast teleporters; hazard biomes place two extra hazards per wave (was one)

2.4.0: 7 weapons instead of 21 — the 14 weapons of the 2.0–2.2 packs were variants of the originals; saves that owned one get that original plus the price difference in shards (or the full price if they own it), selected weapon and unfinished run follow, a toast says what changed; their 12 evolutions and the 15/20-weapon milestones are gone, Full Spectrum needs 4 weapons, World Walker wave 21
2.4.0: double-tapping the move side no longer dashes; the DASH button (Space/Shift on a keyboard) does
